item.text:
**4B.2 Research Note: Ali Khamenei (2024)**

**Bottom line:** I found strong evidence that Khamenei’s system manipulated electoral rules through hard-line vetting and candidate exclusion. I did not find credible evidence that he refrained from such manipulation. The closest “counter-signal” is that a narrow, carefully vetted contest still occurred, but that does not amount to non-manipulation.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Iran’s presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879 | Reuters said Khamenei ensured candidates sharing his hard-line views dominated the contest, and the Guardian Council approved five hardliners and only one low-profile moderate from an initial pool of 80. This is strong evidence of rule manipulation to entrench loyalists. | 4B.2; also 4B.1, 3B.4 |
| [Iran election turnout drops to 41% as reformists criticise poll](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/02/iran-election-turnout-drops-to-41-as-reformists-criticise-poll) | The Guardian | 2024-03-02 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/02/iran-election-turnout-drops-to-41-as-reformists-criticise-poll | Reformists and centrists were blocked from standing without explanation, and the Guardian Council vetted candidates in a way that left the election effectively a hardliner contest. This supports the view that electoral rules were used to narrow competition. | 4B.2; also 4B.1, 3B.8 |
| [Iran vote turnout hits historic low amid discontent](https://www.theprint.in/world/iran-vote-turnout-hits-historic-low-amid-discontent/1986385/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-02 | https://www.theprint.in/world/iran-vote-turnout-hits-historic-low-amid-discontent/1986385/ | Reuters said the parliamentary election was seen as a legitimacy test and was largely a contest between hardliners and low-key conservatives loyal to revolutionary ideals, with turnout around 41%. That is consistent with managed competition rather than a genuinely open process. | 4B.2; also 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.10 |
| [Unofficial reports put Iran election turnout around 40%](https://www.theprint.in/world/unofficial-reports-put-iran-election-turnout-around-40/1985915/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-02 | https://www.theprint.in/world/unofficial-reports-put-iran-election-turnout-around-40/1985915/ | Reuters reported the election was “essentially among hardliners and low-key conservatives,” with heavyweight moderates and conservatives staying out and reformists calling it unfree and unfair. This is direct evidence against genuine non-manipulation. | 4B.2; also 4B.1, 3B.8 |

**On the other side**
- I did not find credible evidence that Khamenei refrained from manipulating electoral rules or state institutions in 2024.
- The closest neutral fact is that the regime still held elections and allowed a narrow slate including one moderate, but the sources above show that slate was tightly filtered and not meaningfully competitive.

**Search gap**
- No reliable 2024 evidence surfaced showing Khamenei genuinely stayed out of candidate vetting, courts, media, election administration, security force pressure, or public-resource favoritism.
- The record I found points in one direction: managed elections and loyalist entrenchment.
